experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, and spices. Sample street foods like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided food walk helps you discover hidden gems and learn about Greek culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm waters, and relax in one of Greece's most beautiful natural settings. Easily accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania to learn how to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and homemade baklava. Classes are typically held in a traditional stone house and include a market visit to source fresh local ingredients, followed by a communal meal with local wine.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Santorini Caldera Taverna
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset while dining at a cliffside taverna overlooking the volcanic caldera. Enjoy fresh grilled octopus, fava dip, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko white wine as the sky turns shades of orange and pink. This is the quintessential Greek island dining experience combining stunning scenery with exceptional local cuisine.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus (€6) to Piraeus Port or the Metro Line 3 to central Athens (€9). Check into a budget hostel near Monastiraki or Omonia for a one-night stopover before heading to Zakynthos. Take a gentle stroll around Monastiraki Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the lively Monastiraki Flea Market area and enjoy the sunset views toward the Acropolis. Grab a cold freddo espresso at a local café and decompress from the journey.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a gyros wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki for €2.50–€3.50 — quick, filling, and authentically Greek.
meals.dinner: Head to Thanasis or Savvas on Mitropoleos Street for affordable souvlaki platters (€8–€10). Sit outside and soak up the atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Book an overnight ferry or early morning flight to Zakynthos in advance. The Ktel bus from Athens to Kyllini port + ferry to Zakynthos is the cheapest route (~€25 total). Alternatively, budget airlines like Ryanair or Sky Express fly Athens–Zakynthos for ~€30–€50. Confirm your Navagio Beach boutique stay check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens early by bus to Kyllini Port (approx. 3.5 hours via KTEL Kyllinis, ~€15). Board the ferry to Zakynthos Town (approx. 1.5 hours, ~€8). Arrive in Zakynthos Town by midday. Pick up a rental scooter or ATV (€15–€25/day) — the most budget-friendly way to explore the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north toward Navagio Beach area and check into your Boutique Stay. Freshen up, then head down to the nearby Agios Nikolaos Beach (accessible by road) for your first swim in the warm Ionian Sea. The water is crystal clear and calm — perfect for cooling off after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small village of Volimes near Navagio — a charming hilltop village known for local honey, textiles, and cheese. Watch the sunset from the Navagio Viewpoint (Shipwreck Lookout) for one of the most iconic views in Greece — completely free.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a bakery in Zakynthos Town for €2–€3 before boarding the ferry.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic of local bread, olives, and feta from a mini-market in Zakynthos Town (€4–€5 total).
meals.dinner: Dine at a local taverna in Volimes village. Try the lamb kleftiko or fresh grilled fish with horta (wild greens) and house wine. Budget €12–€15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach itself is only accessible by boat — plan a boat trip for Day 3. The viewpoint above is free and open 24/7. Rent your scooter/ATV for multiple days to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Join a shared boat excursion from Agios Nikolaos Port to the famous Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach. Shared boat tours cost around €15–€20 per person and typically include stops at the Blue Caves as well. Arrive early (depart by 9:00) to beat the crowds at this iconic beach. Swim, snorkel, and explore the famous rusted shipwreck up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: The boat tour usually includes a stop at the stunning Blue Caves on the north coast — natural sea caves with electric-blue water caused by light refraction. Swim inside the caves and take in the surreal colors. Return to port by early afternoon. Spend the rest of the afternoon relaxing on the quieter Makris Gialos Beach near your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio viewpoint at golden hour for photographs without the daytime crowds. The light at sunset is spectacular. Head back to Volimes or a nearby village for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt with local thyme honey and walnuts from a nearby mini-market or your accommodation (€3–€4).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat trip — local olives, bread, and a piece of graviera cheese (€4–€5). Most boat tours allow you to bring your own food.
meals.dinner: Try Taverna Navagio or a local spot in Anafonitria village. Order the fresh catch of the day with a Greek salad and local white wine. €13–€16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat excursion the evening before or early morning at Agios Nikolaos Port. Shared tours are significantly cheaper than private charters. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water, and a snorkel mask if you have one (or rent one cheaply at the port).

day_by_day.morning: Ride your scooter south to explore the Zakynthos interior. Visit the Byzantine Museum in Zakynthos Town (€4 entry) to learn about the island's rich history and see impressive post-earthquake reconstructions of Venetian-era art. Stroll along the elegant Venetian-style waterfront promenade (Strata Marina).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banana Beach (Agios Sostis area) in the south of the island — one of the longest and most beautiful beaches on Zakynthos, with golden sand and shallow warm water. It's free to access; just rent a sunbed if desired (€5–€7 for two). Swim and relax through the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zakynthos Town in the evening when locals come alive. Visit the main Solomos Square, named after the poet who wrote the Greek national anthem. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and browse the local shops.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a traditional kafeneio (coffee house) in Zakynthos Town for a Greek coffee and a koulouri sesame ring (€2).
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh souvlaki or a gyros pita from a local grill near the waterfront in Zakynthos Town (€3–€4).
meals.dinner: Dine at Malanos Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — a beloved local institution known for affordable, authentic Zakynthian cuisine. Try the sofrito (veal in garlic wine sauce) or rabbit stifado. €12–€15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town was almost entirely rebuilt after the devastating 1953 earthquake, giving it a unique neoclassical-Venetian character. The town is very walkable once you park your scooter. Fuel up your scooter in town as petrol stations are sparse in the north.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Laganas Bay area in the south, home to the National Marine Park of Zakynthos — critical nesting habitat for the endangered loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Walk along Laganas Beach in the early morning when you may spot turtle tracks in the sand from overnight nesting. Visit the Marine Park information center (free entry) to learn about conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at Gerakas Beach, a protected turtle nesting beach with incredibly clear water and a beautiful natural setting. This is one of the best snorkeling spots on the island. Note that swimming is restricted in certain zones to protect nests — follow all signage. The beach itself is stunning and free to visit.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back north along the scenic west coast road, stopping at any viewpoints that catch your eye. Enjoy a quiet evening near your accommodation in the Navagio area. Watch the stars — light pollution is minimal in this part of the island.

meals.breakfast: Make a simple breakfast at your accommodation if facilities allow — local bread, honey, and fruit from the mini-market (€3–€4).
meals.lunch: Stop at a beachside snack bar near Gerakas for a toasted sandwich (tost) and fresh-squeezed orange juice (€5–€6).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal or pick up ready-made mezedes (dips, olives, stuffed vine leaves) from a local deli or mini-market in Volimes. Enjoy on your accommodation terrace with a cold local beer. €6–€8 total.

day_by_day.notes: Turtle nesting season runs May–August. Never approach, disturb, or photograph turtles on the beach. Stay on marked paths. The Marine Park is free but donations are welcome. Gerakas Beach has a strict no-vehicles, no-sunbeds, no-umbrellas policy to protect nests.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike along the clifftop trail near Navagio Beach. The trail offers breathtaking views over the shipwreck bay and the surrounding turquoise Ionian Sea. The walk is moderate and takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. Bring water and wear good shoes. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Porto Limnionas, a stunning rocky cove on the west coast with crystal-clear deep water — perfect for cliff jumping and snorkeling. It's a local favorite and largely undiscovered by mass tourism. Free access.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the village of Keri in the far south for the famous Keri Lighthouse sunset. The lighthouse sits on dramatic cliffs above the sea with views stretching to Marathonisi (Turtle Island). A magical spot at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a hearty breakfast at your boutique stay or a nearby café — scrambled eggs, local bread, and Greek coffee (€4–€5).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Porto Limnionas — local cheese, tomatoes, olives, and crusty bread from Volimes mini-market (€5).
meals.dinner: Dine at Taverna Keri near the lighthouse area. Fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a carafe of house rosé wine with views over the cliffs. €14–€18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Porto Limnionas has no facilities — bring everything you need including water, snacks, and sunscreen. The cliffs are slippery when wet so exercise caution. The Keri Lighthouse road is narrow but manageable on a scooter.

day_by_day.morning: Take a relaxed morning — sleep in, enjoy your accommodation, and read on the terrace. This is your mid-trip rest day. Wander around the Navagio area on foot and visit the small Church of Agios Georgios in Anafonitria village, a 15th-century monastery with a tranquil courtyard. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Navagio Beach via the afternoon boat from Agios Nikolaos Port (boats run multiple times daily, ~€10–€15 return). This time, spend longer swimming, exploring the shipwreck, and simply enjoying one of the world's most beautiful beaches at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a slow sunset evening back at your accommodation. Pick up local Zakynthian mandolato (nougat candy) and pasteli (sesame honey bars) from a shop in Volimes as sweet treats. Relax, journal, and recharge.

meals.breakfast: A lazy breakfast of local yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit. Pick up supplies from the mini-market the night before (€3–€4).
meals.lunch: Bring your own picnic to Navagio Beach — the boat allows cooler bags. Pack cold water, sandwiches, and fruit (€5–€6).
meals.dinner: Simple and satisfying: pick up fresh-made spanakopita (spinach pie) and tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery in Volimes, plus a cold Mythos beer (€5–€7 total). Eat on your terrace under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to observe local Greek life — many families gather for long lunches at tavernas. If you attend a church service at Agios Georgios, dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered). This is a good day to do laundry and reorganize your bag.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Zakynthos and travel to Kefalonia, the largest Ionian island. Take the ferry from Zakynthos Town to Pessada or Argostoli (check current ferry schedules — routes vary seasonally, ~€10–€15). Arrive in Kefalonia by midday. Rent a scooter or use local buses (KTEL Kefalonia) to get around.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head straight to Myrtos Beach — widely considered one of the most spectacular beaches in Greece. The dramatic white pebble beach is framed by towering limestone cliffs and the water is an almost unreal shade of turquoise. Swim and marvel at the scenery. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the charming village of Assos, a tiny peninsula village with a Venetian castle ruin above it. Walk up to the castle (free) for panoramic views of the bay. Watch the sunset from the castle walls — utterly romantic and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a bakery in Zakynthos Town before boarding the ferry (€3).
meals.lunch: There's a small snack bar at Myrtos Beach — grab a sandwich or a Greek salad (€6–€8). Alternatively, bring your own supplies.
meals.dinner: Dine in Assos village at one of the small family-run tavernas. Try the local Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) or fresh grilled fish. €12–€15 per person with local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has strong currents — swim with caution and stay within safe zones. The road down to Myrtos is steep and winding — manageable on a scooter but take it slowly. Book budget accommodation in Argostoli or Fiskardo area in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Melissani Lake Cave near Sami — a magical underground lake inside a collapsed cave where sunlight pours through the open roof and turns the water brilliant shades of blue and emerald. Boat tours inside the cave cost €7–€9 per person. Go early to catch the best light (around 11:00–13:00 the light is most dramatic).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Melissani, head to nearby Antisamos Beach — a gorgeous pebble beach surrounded by lush green hills (famously used in the film 'Captain Corelli's Mandolin'). The water is exceptionally clear. Free access. Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Argostoli, the island's capital, for the evening. Walk along the lively Lithostroto pedestrian street, browse local shops, and watch the loggerhead sea turtles that regularly visit the harbor (best seen at dusk — completely free and magical).

meals.breakfast: Fresh loukoumades (Greek honey doughnuts) from a street vendor or café in Sami (€3).
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for Antisamos Beach — local bread, feta, tomatoes, and olives (€4–€5).
meals.dinner: Dine at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in Argostoli. Order a selection of small dishes — taramosalata, grilled halloumi, dolmades, and saganaki. Share and enjoy with local Robola white wine (Kefalonia's famous grape). €13–€16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Melissani Cave is closed on certain days — verify opening hours in advance. The cave is genuinely one of Greece's most impressive natural wonders. Robola wine is produced only on Kefalonia and is excellent value — pick up a bottle from a local shop (€6–€8).

day_by_day.morning: Hike or drive up to Mount Ainos National Park — the highest peak in the Ionian Islands (1,628m). The mountain is covered in a unique forest of Kefalonian fir trees found nowhere else on Earth. The drive to the summit area offers stunning panoramic views over the entire island and neighboring islands. Free entry to the national park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to the picturesque village of Fiskardo in the far north of the island — the only village that survived the 1953 earthquake intact, preserving its original Venetian architecture. Stroll the charming harbor lined with colorful boats and elegant old buildings. Window-shop and enjoy the atmosphere (Fiskardo is upscale — just enjoy it without spending much).
day_by_day.evening: Find a quiet spot on the rocks near Fiskardo harbor to watch the sunset over the Ionian Sea toward Lefkada island. The light is golden and the scenery is magical. Drive back south to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast at your accommodation or a local café — Greek coffee, bread with local thyme honey (€3–€4).
meals.lunch: Buy supplies from a mini-market in Fiskardo — local cheese, bread, and a cold drink. Eat on the harbor wall (€5–€6). Avoid the restaurants in Fiskardo itself as they cater to yacht tourists and are expensive.
meals.dinner: Return to Argostoli or your accommodation area for dinner. Try Taverna Patsouras in Argostoli — a beloved local spot with excellent Kefalonian cuisine at reasonable prices. €11–€14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The road to Mount Ainos summit is unpaved in sections — a scooter can manage but take it slowly. Bring a light jacket as it's noticeably cooler at altitude even in June. Fiskardo is beautiful but pricey — budget travelers should eat elsewhere.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Athens by taking the ferry from Argostoli or Sami to Patras (approx. 3–4 hours, ~€25–€30), then a KTEL bus or train from Patras to Athens (approx. 3 hours, ~€10–€14). Alternatively, fly Kefalonia–Athens on a budget carrier (~€30–€60). Arrive in Athens by early afternoon and check into a budget hostel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Acropolis and Parthenon (€20 entry, or free if under 25 from an EU country). The afternoon light on the marble is beautiful. Explore the Acropolis Museum below (€10 entry) — one of the finest museums in Europe, housing original sculptures from the Parthenon.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the historic Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district, full of neoclassical houses, bougainvillea, and narrow winding streets. Browse the street art in nearby Psyrri district and enjoy the buzzing evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the ferry or grab a koulouri and coffee from a street vendor in Patras or Athens (€2–€3).
meals.lunch: Stop at a souvlaki joint near Monastiraki — Kostas or O Thanasis are legendary and cheap (€3–€4 per wrap).
meals.dinner: Dine in the Psyrri neighborhood at a traditional taverna. Try the oven-baked lamb with roasted potatoes, a Greek salad, and house wine. €12–€15 per person. The area has many options — look for places with handwritten menus and locals eating inside.

day_by_day.notes: The Acropolis combined ticket (€30) covers multiple archaeological sites and is valid for 5 days — worth buying if you plan to visit several sites. Go to the Acropolis in the late afternoon to avoid peak heat and crowds. Book your Athens hostel well in advance for June.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10 entry, included in combined ticket) — the heart of ancient Athenian democracy where Socrates once walked. The Stoa of Attalos museum inside is excellent. Then visit the Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved ancient Greek temple in existence. Stroll through Kerameikos, the ancient cemetery district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Piraeus Port (€1.20) and catch a ferry to the nearby Saronic island of Aegina (approx. 1 hour, ~€8 each way). Visit the remarkably well-preserved Temple of Aphaia (€6 entry) — a stunning Doric temple from 500 BC with panoramic sea views. Swim at Agia Marina Beach on the east coast of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by evening ferry and head back to Athens. Spend the evening at the vibrant Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area or explore the rooftop bars of Monastiraki with views of the illuminated Acropolis.

meals.breakfast: Visit a traditional Athenian bakery for fresh tiropita, spanakopita, and a freddo cappuccino (€3–€4).
meals.lunch: On Aegina, try the island's famous pistachios (buy a bag from a street vendor, €3–€4) and grab a simple lunch of grilled octopus and bread at a harbor taverna in Aegina Town (€8–€10).
meals.dinner: Back in Athens, dine at a mezedopoleio in Monastiraki or Thissio. Order a spread of mezedes — taramosalata, grilled vegetables, meatballs, and pita. €10–€14 per person with local draft beer.

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is easily doable as a half-day trip from Athens — ferries run frequently from Piraeus. The island is also famous for its pistachios, which make great affordable gifts. If time allows, the evening view of the Acropolis lit up from the Thissio or Monastiraki area is spectacular and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a sensory explosion of fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local produce. It's free to walk through and a fantastic insight into everyday Athenian life. Pick up last-minute food souvenirs: local honey, dried herbs, olive oil, or Greek coffee (all very affordable).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry) — the most important archaeological museum in Greece, housing treasures from across the ancient Greek world including the Mask of Agamemnon. Alternatively, take a final stroll through the Kolonaki neighborhood up to Lycabettus Hill for panoramic views over the entire city (free hike or €7 funicular).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) via Metro Line 3 (€9). Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your departure. Reflect on an incredible 13 days exploring the beaches, flavors, and history of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a final proper Greek breakfast — scrambled eggs with feta, village bread, tomatoes, and strong Greek coffee at a café near your hostel (€5–€7).
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki in Athens — make it count. Head to a classic grill house near Monastiraki for a full souvlaki plate with tzatziki, chips, and pita (€8–€10).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or bring your own snacks from the market. Athens Airport has decent food options but at higher prices — grab a sandwich and local snacks from a mini-market before departing (€5–€7).

day_by_day.notes: Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma to the airport takes approximately 40 minutes and costs €9 (valid for 90 minutes, one direction). Keep your transport card loaded. Pack your olive oil and honey in checked luggage (liquids rules apply for carry-on). Leave time for a final Greek coffee at the airport — you'll miss it immediately upon landing home.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Navagio Beach boutique stay (approx 1.5–2 hrs depending on port and ferry). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate area to get your bearings. Enjoy the stunning coastal views near the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby taverna in the Zakynthos village close to your accommodation for a relaxed first dinner. Try local mezedes (small plates) and a glass of Verdea, Zakynthos's indigenous white wine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a snack bar near the port or airport during transit
meals.dinner: Local taverna near accommodation — try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and fresh village salad (horiatiki). Budget approx €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm ferry/taxi transfer in advance. Exchange some euros if needed at the airport. The sea is warm (29°C highs) so pack your swimwear in hand luggage for easy access.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take the short boat trip to the iconic Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — accessible only by sea. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous rusted shipwreck on the white pebble shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel by early afternoon. Relax at the hotel or a nearby beach cove. Optional: rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local operator along the coast to explore sea caves around the cape.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short taxi to the clifftop viewpoint above Navagio Beach for a spectacular sunset. Then dine at a local restaurant in the nearby village.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local mini-market: olives, cheese, bread, and fruit to enjoy on Navagio Beach
meals.dinner: Taverna in Porto Vromi or nearby village — try bourdeto (Zakynthian spicy fish stew) and local white wine. Approx €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips to Navagio depart from Porto Vromi (closest) or Zakynthos Town. Book the morning slot online or through your hotel the evening before. Wear reef-safe sunscreen — the beach is exposed with little shade.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — a series of stunning sea caves where sunlight refracts through the water creating vivid blue hues. Take a local boat excursion departing from Cape Skinari (about 30 min from Navagio area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Agios Nikolaos village on the way back for a swim at its calm, clear beach. Enjoy a long, lazy lunch by the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation. Enjoy a sunset drink on your hotel terrace or a nearby clifftop bar. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Seafood taverna in Agios Nikolaos — fresh grilled sea bream or calamari with lemon and olive oil. Approx €20–28 per person
meals.dinner: Light meal at a local souvlaki spot or mezedopoleio — try loukoumades (Greek honey doughnuts) for dessert. Approx €15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Caves boat trip through your hotel or Porto Vromi operators. Morning is best for the light effects inside the caves. Bring water shoes as entry points can be rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Zakynthos Town (Chora). Walk along the picturesque Venetian-influenced waterfront, visit the Byzantine Museum housing post-Byzantine icons and artworks, and explore the ruins of Zakynthos Castle (Kastro) with panoramic island views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the town's market streets. Browse local shops for Zakynthian specialties: mandolato nougat, pasteli sesame bars, and local olive oil. Stop at a traditional kafeneion for a Greek coffee and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Zakynthos Town before heading back. The town has a lively evening atmosphere with a good selection of mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional restaurant in Zakynthos Town — try sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce, a Zakynthian specialty) with a carafe of house wine. Approx €22–30 per person
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in Zakynthos Town — fresh fish by the kilo or a mixed grill platter. Approx €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town is about 40–45 min by car/taxi from the Navagio area. Arrange a taxi or rent a car for the day for flexibility. The Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays — check opening days.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or car and drive along the scenic northern coastal road. Stop at Xigia Beach, famous for its natural sulfur springs that bubble up through the sea floor — said to have therapeutic properties. Swim in the warm, slightly sulfurous water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Makris Gialos Beach near the Vassilikos peninsula (southern Zakynthos) for a classic sandy beach afternoon. The water is calm, clear, and ideal for snorkeling. Sun loungers and umbrellas available for rent.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward your accommodation via the west coast road for scenic views. Stop at a village taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery stop en route — fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Makris Gialos — toasted sandwiches, Greek salad, cold drinks. Approx €12–18 per person
meals.dinner: Village taverna on the return route — try rabbit stifado (slow-cooked rabbit with onions) or lamb chops with roasted potatoes. Approx €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The sulfur smell at Xigia is strong but normal. Rinse off afterward. Renting a scooter costs approx €25–35/day; a small car €40–60/day. Book in advance in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at or near your Navagio accommodation. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a slow walk along the coastal path. Optional: yoga or stretching session on the clifftops with sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or family-run winery in the Zakynthos interior for an informal tasting. Many small producers welcome visitors — ask your hotel to arrange an introduction to a local family producer.
day_by_day.evening: Cook-at-home evening (if accommodation has facilities) or a final local dinner in the Navagio/Porto Vromi area. Buy ingredients from a local market: fresh tomatoes, feta, olives, bread, and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Long hotel breakfast — make the most of the spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch during the winery/olive grove visit — typically bread, cheese, olives, and wine are offered as part of the experience
meals.dinner: Self-catered picnic on the terrace or a simple taverna dinner. Approx €15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately slow day to recharge mid-trip. Zakynthos produces excellent Verdea wine and high-quality olive oil — both make great souvenirs to bring home.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: check out of Navagio accommodation and take the ferry from Zakynthos to Kyllini on the Peloponnese mainland (approx 1 hr ferry), then travel onward or take a domestic flight/bus toward Athens or your next destination. Alternatively, take a short flight from Zakynthos Airport to Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Athens. Check in to a mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood — both well-located and full of character. Drop bags and take a first walk through the Plaka district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Monastiraki Square and the surrounding streets. Browse the flea market stalls (open late). Enjoy dinner in a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel or café breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Snack during transit — airport or ferry café, or pack food from a local mini-market
meals.dinner: Rooftop taverna in Monastiraki — try lamb souvlaki, grilled halloumi, and a cold Mythos beer. Approx €22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry or flight from Zakynthos to Athens well in advance. Domestic flights take ~45 min; ferry + bus takes 4–5 hrs. Koukaki and Monastiraki are excellent Athens base neighborhoods for mid-range budgets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon — arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Propylaea, Erechtheion, and Temple of Athena Nike. Then visit the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Ancient Agora and Temple of Hephaestus. Stroll through the Thissio neighborhood and enjoy a coffee break at a café overlooking the archaeological site.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Psyrri neighborhood for Athens's vibrant street art scene and bar culture. Have dinner at a traditional ouzeri.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel — Greek coffee, bougatsa (custard pastry), and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Plaka — try a gyros pita or a Greek salad at a neighborhood taverna. Approx €10–15 per person
meals.dinner: Ouzeri in Psyrri — order a selection of mezedes: taramosalata, grilled sardines, saganaki (fried cheese), and ouzo or tsipouro. Approx €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy the Acropolis combined ticket (€30) which covers 7 archaeological sites — great value. Wear comfortable walking shoes and a hat. The Acropolis Museum is air-conditioned and excellent — allow 1.5–2 hrs.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Piraeus port and catch a ferry to Hydra island (approx 1.5–2 hrs by high-speed ferry). Hydra is famously car-free — only donkeys and boats. Walk the beautiful harbor and explore the stone mansions and narrow alleyways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a water taxi to one of Hydra's secluded swimming spots — Vlychos Beach or Bisti Beach. Crystal-clear water and peaceful surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Athens (last ferries depart around 17:00–19:00 — check schedule). Dinner near your Athens hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Waterfront restaurant in Hydra Town — try fresh grilled fish, shrimp saganaki, and a glass of local wine. Approx €25–35 per person
meals.dinner: Neighborhood restaurant near Athens hotel — try moussaka or pastitsio (Greek pasta bake) at a family-run taverna. Approx €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets from Piraeus to Hydra: approx €35–50 return (high-speed). Book in advance in June. Hydra has no ATMs that always work — bring cash. Water taxis to beaches cost €5–10 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a vibrant, authentic market with fish, meat, spices, and produce. Fascinating cultural experience. Then explore the Monastiraki flea market for antiques, vintage items, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed walk up Lycabettus Hill (by funicular or on foot) for the best 360-degree panoramic views of Athens and the Acropolis. Ideal in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the upscale but accessible Kolonaki neighborhood — Athens's most stylish quarter. Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast near the market — fresh koulouri sesame ring and a Greek coffee from a market vendor
meals.lunch: Taverna near Monastiraki — try a hearty bean soup (fasolada) or stuffed vine leaves (dolmades) with yogurt. Approx €12–18 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Kolonaki — try modern Greek cuisine: slow-cooked lamb with orzo (giouvetsi), accompanied by a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini. Approx €30–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Varvakios Market is busiest and most atmospheric in the morning. The funicular to Lycabettus runs frequently and costs around €7 return. Kolonaki restaurants fill up — book ahead for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion (70 km south of Athens, 1.5 hr by bus from Pedion Areos). Visit the magnificent Temple of Poseidon perched dramatically on the clifftop above the Aegean. Lord Byron carved his name in the marble — look for it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at one of the small beaches along the Apollo Coast (Athenian Riviera) on the return journey — Vouliagmeni Lake or Varkiza Beach are excellent mid-range options with clear water and good facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens. Light evening walk through Koukaki and Filopappou Hill area. Casual dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Taverna near Cape Sounion — simple fresh fish, Greek salad, and house wine with a sea view. Approx €20–28 per person
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood taverna near hotel — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad) and a mixed grill. Approx €18–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Sounion depart from Pedion Areos (Mavromataion terminal) regularly — approx €7 each way. The site is exposed and very hot midday — visit early and bring water and sunscreen. Combined beach stop makes it a perfect full day.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for last-minute exploration or relaxation. Optional: visit the Benaki Museum (Greek art and history from prehistoric to modern times) or the National Archaeological Museum — one of the world's great collections of ancient Greek artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping in Monastiraki and Plaka. Pick up: local honey, saffron from Kozani, olive oil, mastiha products, Greek herbs, and handmade ceramics. Enjoy a final Greek coffee at a traditional kafeneion.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views — the perfect way to end the trip. Watch the Acropolis light up after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely café breakfast — try avgolemono soup if available, or a full Greek breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Street food tour of Monastiraki — gyros, spanakopita, fresh loukoumades, and a cold frappe. Approx €10–15 per person
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Plaka or Monastiraki — splurge slightly on the farewell meal: lamb chops, seafood, fine Greek wine, and baklava for dessert. Approx €35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Many museums are free on the first Sunday of the month. The National Archaeological Museum requires 2–3 hrs minimum. Pack your bags in the evening and prepare for departure. Keep souvenirs within airline liquid/weight limits.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning. Enjoy a last Greek breakfast at a neighborhood café. Take a slow walk through Plaka one final time if time permits — the streets are quiet and beautiful in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos). Allow at least 2.5–3 hrs before departure. Browse duty-free for any last Greek products: Metaxa brandy, mastiha liqueur, or Greek olive oil.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry wonderful memories of Zakynthos beaches, Navagio's shipwreck, Blue Caves, Athens's ancient wonders, and the incredible flavors of Greek food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek café breakfast — tiropita, Greek yogurt, and a strong Greek coffee. Savor it!
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a final souvlaki from a street vendor near the hotel before checkout
meals.dinner: In-flight or at airport if departure is late evening

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange late checkout or luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. The metro from central Athens to the airport takes about 40 min and costs €10 — convenient and reliable. Take the X95 express bus as an alternative for €6.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to your boutique stay at Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink on your private terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided orientation walk along the clifftops above Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach. Take in the iconic panoramic views of the turquoise cove and the rusted shipwreck below. Your concierge briefs you on the week's curated experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace as the sun dips into the Ionian Sea. Ease into your first evening in Greece with a light, leisurely dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Welcome mezze platter and chilled white wine served in-room or on your private terrace upon arrival — arranged by the hotel.
meals.dinner: In-hotel fine dining: fresh grilled sea bass with lemon-caper butter, Zakynthian salad with local capers and feta, and a bottle of Assyrtiko from Santorini.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in if possible to maximise your first afternoon. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter departing from the hotel's dedicated jetty. Cruise directly to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach before the day-tripper crowds arrive. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters, snorkel around the MV Panagiotis wreck, and enjoy the white-pebble beach in near-total seclusion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour northward along Zakynthos's dramatic limestone coastline. Visit the famous Blue Caves near Cape Skinari — swim inside the sea caves where light refracts into vivid blue hues. The captain serves chilled prosecco and fresh fruit on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by late afternoon. Shower and change for a premium dinner at a clifftop restaurant in the nearby village of Anafonitria, known for its authentic Zakynthian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious buffet breakfast at the hotel: Greek yogurt with Zakynthian honey and walnuts, fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the boat prepared by the hotel kitchen: prosciutto, marinated octopus, artisan bread, local olives, and chilled rosé.
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or equivalent clifftop restaurant: slow-braised lamb with rosemary and local wine, grilled prawns, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts) for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Arrive at Navagio by 8:30am for the best light and fewest visitors. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning yoga or pilates session on the hotel terrace with an in-house instructor, overlooking the Ionian Sea. Follow with a refreshing dip in the infinity pool. A slow, indulgent start to the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided food tour of Zakynthos Town (Zante Town), approximately 40 minutes by private car. Visit the covered market to taste local specialties: mandolato nougat, pasteli sesame bars, local olive oils, and Verdea white wine. Stop at a traditional deli for a curated tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zakynthos Town at a premium harbourfront restaurant. Watch the boats drift in as the evening light turns golden over the port.

meals.breakfast: À la carte hotel breakfast: eggs Benedict with smoked local trout, fresh fruit platter, Greek coffee, and freshly baked tiropita (cheese pie).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a traditional kafeneion in Zakynthos Town: dakos (rusk salad), spanakopita, and a glass of local Verdea wine.
meals.dinner: Harbourfront fine dining: grilled whole lobster with garlic and herb butter, stuffed calamari with rice and herbs, and a premium bottle of Ktima Mercouri white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Private car and driver should be arranged through the hotel. The food tour guide can be pre-booked through the concierge for a personalised experience. Zakynthos Town is most pleasant in the early evening when locals come out for their volta (evening stroll).

day_by_day.morning: Private snorkelling and sea-kayaking excursion along the secluded northern coastline of Zakynthos. Paddle through sea arches and hidden coves only accessible by water. A professional guide accompanies you and points out marine life including sea turtles (Zakynthos is a key nesting site for loggerhead turtles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit to the Zakynthos Marine Park information centre near Laganas Bay (private car transfer). Learn about the loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) conservation programme. Optional guided walk along a protected beach where turtle nests may be visible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-room or terrace spa treatment: traditional Greek aromatherapy massage using local olive oil and herbs. Followed by a quiet dinner under the stars on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey, granola, and seasonal berries; fresh-pressed juice; and a traditional Greek omelette with feta and tomatoes.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed on the kayak tour: wraps with grilled chicken, tzatziki, and roasted vegetables; chilled sparkling water and local fruit.
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the hotel: grilled swordfish with capers and sun-dried tomatoes, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a chilled bottle of Gaia Thalassitis Assyrtiko.

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle nesting season runs June–August; respect all marine park rules — no flash photography near nests and maintain distance from turtles. The spa treatment should be booked 24 hours in advance with the hotel wellness team.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter or small seaplane transfer from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (approximately 20 minutes), offering breathtaking aerial views of the Ionian Islands. Alternatively, a premium private speedboat transfer (approximately 1.5 hours) for a more scenic sea journey. Check in to a luxury clifftop villa or boutique hotel near Myrtos Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Myrtos Beach — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Greece and the Mediterranean. Swim in the vivid turquoise water against a backdrop of dramatic white limestone cliffs. Lounge on a premium sunbed with dedicated beach service.
day_by_day.evening: Drive up to the clifftop viewpoint above Myrtos Beach at golden hour for one of the most spectacular sunsets in Greece. Then head to the charming village of Assos for a waterfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Zakynthos hotel before departure: full Greek spread including local cheeses, honey, pastries, eggs, and cold cuts.
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Myrtos: fresh seafood salad, grilled octopus, and chilled white wine served directly to your sunbed.
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in Assos village: fresh catch of the day, grilled with lemon and olive oil; local Robola wine from Kefalonia's celebrated vineyards.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter or seaplane transfers must be booked well in advance — coordinate through your travel concierge. Robola is Kefalonia's signature grape variety and should not be missed. Assos is a small, picturesque village — arrive by 7:30pm to secure a good table.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Melissani Cave Lake — an extraordinary underground lake where sunlight streams through a collapsed roof, illuminating the water in shades of electric blue and turquoise. Arrive early for the best light (around 11:00–12:00 the light is most dramatic). Followed by a visit to the nearby Drogarati Cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kefalonia's interior by private car: drive through the lush green mountains and vineyards to the Gentilini Winery near Argostoli for a premium wine tasting. Sample their organic Robola, Muscat, and red blends with a curated cheese and charcuterie board.
day_by_day.evening: Evening stroll along the waterfront promenade in Argostoli, Kefalonia's charming capital. Watch the famous loggerhead sea turtles that gather in the harbour at dusk. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Argostoli.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: eggs your way, freshly baked bread, local honey, seasonal fruit, and Kefalonian herb tea.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery: artisan charcuterie, aged cheeses, marinated vegetables, and fresh bread paired with Robola white wine.
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant in Argostoli: Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) as a starter, followed by pan-seared sea bream with caramelised fennel, and a Kefalonian Muscat dessert wine with baklava.

day_by_day.notes: Melissani Cave is best visited between 11:00am and 12:30pm when the sun shines directly through the roof opening. Gentilini Winery tastings should be pre-booked. Sea turtles in Argostoli harbour are most visible at dusk near the fish market area.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at leisure on Kefalonia. Optional: private sunrise hike to the summit of Mount Ainos (the island's highest peak at 1,628m) with a local guide for panoramic views of the Ionian Islands — best done early to avoid the heat. Alternatively, a relaxed morning by the hotel pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat excursion to the secluded Antisamos Beach (made famous by the film Captain Corelli's Mandolin). Swim in the deep, clear green-blue water surrounded by lush forested hills. The boat continues to explore hidden sea caves and isolated coves along the northeastern coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel for a private chef experience: a local Kefalonian chef prepares a traditional feast in your villa or on the terrace, explaining each dish and its cultural significance.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the hike (if chosen): Greek yogurt, energy bars, and coffee. Or full hotel breakfast if taking a leisurely morning.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the boat at Antisamos Beach: fresh bread, taramasalata, grilled vegetables, cold cuts, and chilled Assyrtiko.
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner: Kefalonian lamb sofrito, pastitsada (spiced pasta with rooster), fresh village salad, and a selection of local wines and spirits including tsipouro.

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Ainos hike requires sturdy footwear and should begin no later than 6:30am in summer heat. The private chef experience should be arranged 48 hours in advance through your accommodation. This is a wonderful mid-trip highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Premium private ferry or speedboat transfer from Kefalonia to Lefkada (approximately 2–3 hours by fast boat, with stunning island-hopping scenery). Check in to a luxury boutique hotel near Porto Katsiki or Egremni Beach on Lefkada's west coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porto Katsiki Beach — one of Greece's most iconic and dramatic beaches, accessed by steps cut into white limestone cliffs. Swim in the brilliant turquoise water. Arrange a private sunbed and umbrella service through your hotel for a fully exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive north along the west coast to the hilltop village of Kalamitsi for sunset drinks at a clifftop bar with panoramic views. Then descend to the coast for a seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final Kefalonia hotel breakfast before departure: full spread with local specialties, fresh juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach taverna near Porto Katsiki: grilled sardines, village salad, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood restaurant near Lefkada Town or Agios Nikitas: whole grilled red mullet, grilled prawns with garlic, and a chilled bottle of Lefkadian white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki is accessible by steps (approximately 100 steps) or by small boat from the sea. Book your premium boat transfer between islands well in advance. Lefkada is connected to the mainland by a causeway but the sea approach is far more dramatic and luxurious.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing day around Lefkada and the Meganisi island group. Depart early and sail to the stunning beaches of Meganisi — a tiny, unspoiled island with emerald bays and traditional fishing villages. Swim from the boat in crystalline water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at Spilia Bay or Atherinos Beach on Meganisi for a long, lazy lunch on board. Snorkel, paddleboard, or simply float in the warm Ionian water. The catamaran captain navigates to a second secluded bay for afternoon swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back to Lefkada as the sun sets over the water. Cocktails on deck as you watch the sky turn pink and gold. Dinner ashore in the charming village of Nidri or Sivota.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: fresh pastries, Greek yogurt, honey, eggs, and coffee before boarding the catamaran.
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch prepared by the catamaran's private chef: grilled fresh fish, Greek salad, tzatziki, pita, and chilled rosé wine.
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in Nidri or Sivota: grilled lobster spaghetti, fried zucchini blossoms stuffed with feta, and local white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private catamaran charters in Lefkada should be booked through your hotel concierge or a specialist charter company. Meganisi is a hidden gem — far less visited than the main Ionian islands. Bring a light layer for the sail back in the evening breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lefkada Town in the morning: a charming, earthquake-resistant town with distinctive Venetian-influenced architecture and colourful tin-clad buildings. Visit the local market for artisan products — Lefkadian olive oil, local cheeses, and handmade lace (a traditional craft of the island).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Egremni Beach on the west coast — a stunning, remote beach accessible by a long staircase (around 350 steps) or by private boat. This is one of the least crowded premium beaches in the Ionian. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing in complete tranquillity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a premium spa treatment (couples massage or body scrub with local olive oil and sea salt). Light dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: À la carte hotel breakfast: smoked salmon with cream cheese on sourdough, fresh fruit, Greek coffee, and a selection of pastries.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Egremni Beach: prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, local olives, and chilled water.
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or nearby fine dining: slow-roasted pork with honey and thyme, grilled halloumi salad, and a glass of aged Nemea red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Egremni Beach suffered a partial landslide in 2015 but remains accessible and beautiful. The steps are steep — wear good sandals. Alternatively, arrange a private boat drop-off for a truly exclusive experience. Lefkadian lace makes a wonderful premium souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer or short flight back toward Athens or onward to Santorini (depending on your return flight routing). If flying home from Athens, this is a travel morning. If time permits, a brief stop in Athens is recommended. Check in to a premium hotel in Athens (Syntagma or Kolonaki area) or Santorini.
day_by_day.afternoon: If in Athens: Private guided tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon in the afternoon — book a skip-the-line premium tour for an exclusive experience with a licensed archaeologist guide. Alternatively, explore the upscale Kolonaki neighbourhood and its galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop dinner in Athens with a direct view of the illuminated Acropolis — one of the most memorable dining experiences in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final Lefkada hotel breakfast: full Greek spread with local honey, cheeses, eggs, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Athens upon arrival: mezze at a premium restaurant in Monastiraki or Plaka — taramasalata, grilled octopus, fava, and fresh pita.
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Athens (such as a hotel rooftop with Acropolis views): premium Greek tasting menu — 5 courses featuring modern takes on classic Greek dishes, paired with a curated Greek wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and a licensed guide well in advance — the site is extremely popular in June. The rooftop dinner reservation should be made at least 3–4 days ahead. If routing through Santorini instead, adjust accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: If still in Athens: Morning visit to the National Archaeological Museum — one of the world's great museums, housing extraordinary ancient Greek artefacts. Private guided tour recommended for depth and context. Alternatively, explore the upscale Voukourestiou Street for premium Greek designer shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day trip to Cape Sounion (approximately 1 hour from Athens by private car) to visit the Temple of Poseidon perched dramatically on a cliff above the Aegean Sea. Swim at a nearby beach on the Athenian Riviera on the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Athens at a premium restaurant in Kolonaki or Kifissia, celebrating the end of a magnificent Greek journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Athens: full luxury spread — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, Greek yogurt, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on the Athenian Riviera during the Cape Sounion return: fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner: modern Greek cuisine — lamb chops with mint and pomegranate, sea urchin pasta, aged feta with truffle honey, and a premium bottle of Ktima Gerovassiliou Malagousia.

day_by_day.notes: Cape Sounion is best visited in the late afternoon for golden light on the temple columns and a spectacular sunset over the Aegean. The Athenian Riviera (Glyfada, Vouliagmeni) offers excellent premium beach clubs for a midday swim on the return.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Athens. Late checkout arranged through your hotel. Enjoy a final Greek breakfast at a neighbourhood café in Kolonaki — freddo espresso, tiropita, and koulouri (sesame bread ring). Browse a local agora or artisan shop for last-minute premium souvenirs: local olive oil, wine, saffron, and handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos). Allow ample time for departure. Use the premium lounge at the airport for a final relaxed Greek coffee and snack before your flight home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the beaches, flavours, and beauty of the Greek Ionian Islands and Athens.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a Kolonaki café: freddo cappuccino or Greek mountain tea, tiropita, spanakopita, and a koulouri with honey.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch near the hotel or at the airport premium lounge: mezze selection, fresh bread, and a final glass of Greek wine.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (12:00–13:00) from your Athens hotel when booking. Leave at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Consider purchasing premium Greek products at the airport duty-free: Mastiha liqueur, Santorini Assyrtiko wine, and Greek saffron from Kozani are excellent luxury gifts.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC
